- [ ] **Used semantic containers?** (e.g., `HeaderedContainer` instead of `Border` with manual heade
- [ ] **Avoided redundant properties?** Use shared styles in `axaml` files.
- [ ] **Minimized nesting?** Flatten layouts using `EdgePanel` or generic components.
- [ ] **Icons via extension?** Use `{Icon fa-name}` and `IconOptions` for styling.
- [ ] **Behaviors over code-behind?** Use `Interaction.Behaviors` for UI-logic.
- Create deep nesting of `Grid` and `StackPanel`.
- Use `IValueConverter` for simple logic that belongs in the ViewModel.
- Use `DynamicResource` for colors and brushes.
- Leverage `Zafiro.Avalonia` specific panels like `EdgePanel` for common UI patterns.

content.user_title: Build Cleaner Avalonia Layouts with Zafiro
content.value_statement: Avalonia views often become repetitive and deeply nested. This skill applies Zafiro.Avalonia containers, shared styles, behaviors, and reusable components to simplify layout design.
actual_capabilities: Organizes Avalonia colors, brushes, styles, and merged dictionaries into reusable theme resources.
Recommends HeaderedContainer, EdgePanel, and Card patterns for common content structures.
Shows IconExtension and IconOptions usage for consistent icons without unnecessary wrapper controls.
Moves interaction logic into reusable behaviors and discourages simple converters when ViewModel properties suffice.
Identifies repeated or deeply nested XAML and suggests reusable components or flatter panels.
Provides a checklist for reviewing layout consistency and maintainability.
limitations: Guidance targets Avalonia UI projects using Zafiro.Avalonia and may not fit other XAML frameworks.
Examples are conceptual and do not verify installed package versions, namespaces, or project-specific APIs.
The referenced Angor solution path is environment-specific and may not exist for users.
Generated layout changes still require compilation, visual inspection, accessibility checks, and interaction testing.

use_cases.title: Refactor Repetitive Views
use_cases.description: Refactor repetitive views into flatter layouts with shared styles and semantic containers.

use_cases.title: Define UI Conventions
use_cases.description: Define reusable theme resources, container conventions, icon styling, and component boundaries for a growing desktop product.

use_cases.title: Review Layout Quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate pull requests for redundant properties, deep nesting, unnecessary converters, and inconsistent Zafiro.Avalonia usage.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify My First View
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Avalonia XAML: [paste view]. Suggest a simpler layout using Zafiro.Avalonia containers while preserving bindings and behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate Theme Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Avalonia views and theme files: [paste content]. Identify repeated visual properties and propose shared DynamicResource values, classes, and merged dictionaries.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Reusable Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these related views: [paste views]. Find repeated layout patterns, define reusable component responsibilities, and explain where EdgePanel or HeaderedContainer fits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit UI Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Avalonia UI area: [describe files and goals]. Assess theme organization, component granularity, behaviors, icons, nesting, and Zafiro.Avalonia container choices. Prioritize recommendations by impact and migration effort.

output_examples.input: A settings view repeats bordered sections and manually aligns every label with its action.
output: Replace repeated bordered sections with HeaderedContainer variants.
Move recurring colors, spacing, and border values into shared theme resources.
Use EdgePanel for rows with leading labels and trailing actions.

output_examples.input: Three screens repeat the same summary row with different labels, values, and icons.
output_examples.output: Create one reusable summary component with label, value, and icon inputs. Apply a shared class so all instances use the same visual treatment.

output_examples.input: A view uses several converters for display text, visibility, and focus behavior.
output: Expose final display values and simple state properties from the ViewModel.
Keep only conversions that are purely visual and broadly reusable.
Move focus handling into a reusable interaction behavior.

best_practices: Provide the relevant views, theme files, installed Zafiro.Avalonia version, and visual goals.
Preserve bindings, accessibility semantics, and interaction behavior while simplifying layout structure.
Compile and visually test every recommendation across supported themes, sizes, and platforms.
anti_patterns: Do not apply Zafiro.Avalonia patterns to projects that do not use the library.
Do not replace clear native controls when a specialized container adds no practical value.
Do not accept generated XAML without checking namespaces, package compatibility, bindings, and runtime behavior.

faq.question: What does this skill improve?
faq.answer: It improves Avalonia layout structure, theme reuse, component design, icon consistency, and interaction organization.

faq.question: Does my project need Zafiro.Avalonia?
faq.answer: Yes, the container and icon recommendations assume Zafiro.Avalonia. General advice about styles and component reuse can still apply elsewhere.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete view?
faq.answer: It can propose view structures and patterns, but you must integrate namespaces, packages, bindings, and project-specific behavior.

faq.question: Does it eliminate all converters?
faq.answer: No. It discourages simple business or formatting logic in converters but accepts reusable conversions that are purely visual.

faq.question: Can it help organize light and dark themes?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends shared colors, brushes, DynamicResource references, grouped styles, and merged resource dictionaries.

faq.question: How should I validate its recommendations?
faq.answer: Compile the application, inspect each supported theme and window size, test interactions, and verify accessibility behavior.
